liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dancin' In The Street** (3 reviews): Jam is tight and jazzy, with strong vocals; Bob called it unexpectedly; Jerry later said on a hotel interview tape that the band didn't know the song [11][12][13]
- **Lazy Lightning** (3 reviews): Jam is described as tight and jazzy; The Lazy Lightning into Supplication jam is named a highlight of the set [11][20][21]
- **El Paso** (2 reviews): The band seems to lose its way during El Paso [20][21]
- **Supplication** (2 reviews): Jerry plays fast, impressive lead lines here; Reviewer finds Supplication very good, after an unimpressive start to the show [12][18]
- **Minglewood Blues** (1 review): The Minglewood into Bertha opening rocks [13]

## Setlist highlights

- **Dancin' In The Street**: back after 138 archived shows (575 days) [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-07-07.mtx.sirmick.110637.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 167 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd81-07-07.sbd.miller.30649.sbeok.flacf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 164 min; rated 2.57/5 by 7 [3]. Said about its sound: This newer soundboard is rated a B+ source; Sound quality is not great [18][19]
- **gd1981-07-07.175191.sbd.miller.phase.repair.flac1644**: soundboard; 23 songs; 164 min [4]
- **gd81-07-07.neumann.munder.13962.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 162 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [5]. Said about its sound: Audience recording sounds cavernous with noticeable crowd noise, yet is fairly clear [15]
- **gd1981-07-07.176356.aud.bernstein.ackerman.noel.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 164 min [6]

## Around the show

- First set has a three-song opening run and a three-song closing run that suit it well [19]
- Reviewer links the heavier blues-rock sound of Jerry and Brent to the first set at Long Beach in 1981 [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-07-07.mtx.sirmick.110637.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by SIRMick; source: Matrix 60% sbd/40% aud SBD -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Dat (shnid 109850) and Aud (Neumann KMi84's)>MC>DAT>CD (shnid 13962) [1]. Also: Audience recording was missing the start of Lazy Lightning and the end of Looks Like Rain; both were patched in; About 27 seconds of Drums missing from the audience tape were patched in from the soundboard [1]
- **gd81-07-07.sbd.miller.30649.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard [3]
- **gd1981-07-07.175191.sbd.miller.phase.repair.flac1644**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  November 20, 2025; source: SBD > Cassette Master > Reel > DAT [4]. Also: Uploader repaired a vocal phase problem on another soundboard transfer, using pitch correction settings from Joe B. Jones [4]
- **gd81-07-07.neumann.munder.13962.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: Neumann KM184's [5]
- **gd1981-07-07.176356.aud.bernstein.ackerman.noel.flac2496**: taped by Jon Bernstein; transferred by Transfer & Mastering by Ray Ackerman Edited & Processed w/ add'l Mastering by Joe Noel January 24, 2026; source: ?? mics > ?? lead deck > Sony TC-D5 > Master Cassettes (Maxell XLIIS-90's) [6]. Also: Taper Jon Bernstein recorded from front of board, centered; Ray Ackerman did the transfer; Brian Schley supplied the patch source [6]

## Art and photos

- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1981-07-07 Tue Music Hall (Municipal Auditorium), Kansas City, MO](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1279714036512/grateful-dead-1981-07-07-tue-music-hall) [23]
